classification.difficultyReason: Relate one, two and zero horizontal-line intersections to levels equal to, above and below the labelled minimum ordinate.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows the graph of a function $y=f(x)$, and a horizontal line $y=k$. Find the value(s) of $k$ such that $f(x)=k$ has

spec.description: Upward-opening blue parabola with vertex on the y-axis at -1, and a red horizontal line above the x-axis crossing both branches. Labels match their series. There are no x ticks, grid or numerical labels for the horizontal level. Source series colours are mapped to standard accents.
spec.mathematics: The function has minimum ordinate -1. The unnumbered horizontal scale and unnumbered displayed level are schematic; the plotting parameterisation does not supply an additional function rule or value of k.
spec.answerVisibility: The given minimum ordinate and series labels remain visible; the three requested parameter conditions appear only in answers.

answer.worked: There is one intersection when the horizontal line passes through the vertex. The vertex has ordinate $-1$, so $k=-1$.
A horizontal line above the minimum meets both branches of the parabola. Hence $k>-1$.
A horizontal line below the minimum does not meet the parabola. Hence $k<-1$.
